\section{Related work}
The line-breaking algorithm follows Knuth and Plass~\cite{plass81}; the
page builder follows the description in \emph{The \TeX book}~\cite{knuth84}.
Incremental recomputation over a block cache is standard in build systems
and editors~\cite{adapton}; what differs here is that the cost model being
replayed is TeX's own.

\section{Conclusion}
The two mechanisms introduced in Sections~\ref{sec:intro} and
\ref{sec:method} are independent: the cache can be disabled without changing
output, and the page builder can be driven by a batch compiler. That
separation is what makes the pixel comparison in the appendix meaningful.

\appendix
\section{Measurement protocol}\label{app:protocol}
Every document is compiled twice by pdfLaTeX with a fixed
\texttt{SOURCE\_DATE\_EPOCH}, then rasterised at 144 dpi. The producer's
PDF is rasterised the same way and differing pixels are counted per page.
Page counts are compared first; a page-count mismatch is reported as such
and no pixel count is claimed for the missing pages.
